chapter: Pedal points, Hampton, Norvo and Debut
title: Boyd Raeburn's band and Harry Babasin
summary: Mingus was in Raeburn's band, threw down his bass over a syncopated part, recommended others, and never lasted with leaders.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: You ever hear Boyd Rayburn play "Boyd Meets Stravinsky?"
at one point. Boyd Raeburn's band Floyd Raeburn's piano got Britt on band. I didn't know Britt was on that band.
I do, too. I (inaudible) that man.
: yeah, I heard something -- Yeah, I got him on that band.
(Inaudible) -- Well, I was in the band with him, man, I was in the band before Britt. That's how Britt got in the band, because Harry Battles had come over and stood

behind my back when I was -- in those days, I was studying, I could read very well, except syncopation was a little rough on me, the classical (inaudible) syncopation like that. (Singing.) That's what the bass part looked like. So Harry Battles was going to help me. "Hey, man, look, you should do that this way." I said, "Fuck it, man," and threw the bass down. I said, "You're probably going to say I got real paranoid and remember the saying Negroes can't read." (Inaudible) said, "I got a guy can outread any two guys outread anything, trombone player -- Buddy Collette on alto, (inaudible) on the trombone. So I went and called; Buddy (inaudible), I got Rick Boyd to come out. Britt came out and Floyd hired him. But I didn't go in the band.
Somehow or another, it's hard to imagine you working for anybody else very long.
I never did make it through that.
